topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and establishes its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations, susceptibility and clonal evolution in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support cancer development through clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk against explanations based on chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of cooperating infectious influences.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion before tumours develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure affects carcinogenic susceptibility and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of cancer causation.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenic activity is obtained and why its interpretation is constrained by the biological context of cancer development.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing synthesises the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and carcinogen assessment around everyday risk–benefit decisions.
